p-value of the T1 average marginal effect (Democratic White Women vs Republican White Men, COVID model), column p of summary(margins(...))
targets.note: Pre-registered quantity is the AME p from summary(margins(...)): reproduced 0.056899, which rounds to 0.057, not 0.054. The quasi-Poisson coefficient p for Democratic White Women from summary(covid) (t test, dispersion 17.0501), printed by the authors' own code in outputs/multivariate_full_run.log, is 0.054230, which rounds to 0.054 and equals the paper's 0.054. Observation only: the paper's 'p = .054' matches the coefficient p, not the AME p; the paper's conclusion band (0.05 <= p < 0.10) holds for both.

bugs.description: Hard-coded sample-size labels in the detailed race and ethnicity chunk do not match the deposited data (labels only; the means in that table and all model estimates are unaffected). Line 1094 hard-codes freq c(335,102,42,52,48,46,19,4,2,1,1,1) and line 1095 labels 'Black Men (n=42)', 'Black Women (n=52)', 'Latino Men (n=48)', 'Latina Woman (n=46)', 'Asian Women (n=4)', 'Middle Eastern Men (n=1)'.
bugs.evidence: table(by_leg$race_gender) in outputs/group_counts_check.txt gives Black Man 44, Black Woman 50, Latino Man 47, Latina Woman 47, Asian American Woman 5, Middle Eastern Man 2 (White Woman 101, matching the label but not freq 102). race_gender is a factor whose level order equals the label order, so group_by rows align with labels; the labels appear in the authors' output outputs/meansbyraceandgenderandethnicity.doc. Not used by any target.

env_fixes: diffs/README.md: created the three output folders the code writes to (no authors' file edited)
diffs/README.md: rtweet installed as Debian binary r-cran-rtweet 2.0.0, so library(rtweet) ran unchanged (no comment-out needed)
class_reason: Strict reading: targets not matching to rounding: T4. T1, T2, T3, T5, T6 match the paper to rounding (and the authors' own A8/A10 html outputs reproduce the published cells), but T4 as pre-registered (AME p from summary(margins)) is 0.0569 vs the paper's 0.054 (rel diff 5.4%, outside 5%, same conclusion band), so neither A nor B applies and D does not apply (conclusion unchanged); the source of the text's p = .054 is unclear from the code, as it equals the coefficient p (0.0542), hence C. Alternative: A if T4 is read as the coefficient p.
confidence_reason: All numbers matched by script and the full authors' pipeline ran without error, but the class turns on a judgement about which p-value the text's .054 reports; package versions are not pinned by the authors.
uncertainties: T4: the pre-registered AME p (0.0569) differs from the paper's .054 by more than 5% relative; the coefficient t-test p (0.0542) printed by the authors' code equals .054. Which quantity the text reports cannot be confirmed from the deposit; this drives the C vs A proposal.

Package versions: none pinned by the authors; run used R 4.5.0, margins 0.3.28, prediction 0.3.18 (Debian), texreg 1.40 (see environment.txt). Exact agreement of A8 and A10 cells suggests drift is not material.
R_a bootstrap and R_c negative binomial change the significance pattern for some groups (see robustness notes); robustness does not change the class.
Time-Series Analysis.Rmd (glmer models, Table 1, A16 to A20) was not run; PREREG says it is not needed for any target.
Sage supplementary ZIP was not checked by agent B (not needed; Dataverse deposit holds every file the code reads).
R_a 'same_direction_and_significance_as_paper' for the primary estimate uses the PREREG rule: percentile 95% CI excludes 0.
